subject: orthopaedics
title: Leg, ankle and foot injuries: high-yield eponyms and key signs

steps.tx: The **ankle** is one of the commonest sites of acute injury, and sprains make up most cases. The **anterior talofibular ligament** is the most commonly injured lateral ligament, followed by the calcaneofibular and then the posterior talofibular ligament. The posterior talofibular ligament is the strongest and is rarely torn. Inversion injuries also cause peroneal tendon damage and avulsion fractures of the lateral malleolus.

rows: Ankle instability when combined with ATFL

steps.tx: **Danis-Weber** classification grades ankle fractures by the level of the fibular fracture relative to the syndesmosis. Type A lies below the syndesmosis, Type B lies at the level of the syndesmosis, and Type C lies above it, where the ankle mortise is unstable. The **Tillaux fracture** is an anterolateral avulsion of the distal tibial epiphysis, a Salter-Harris type III injury in adolescents, caused by the anterior tibiofibular ligament.

steps.tx: A **Bohler angle** is measured on the lateral calcaneal radiograph, normally about 20 to 40 degrees. Flattening of this angle is a classic sign of a depressed calcaneal fracture. The **crucial angle of Gissane** normally measures about 100 degrees and increases in intra-articular calcaneal fractures. Calcaneal fractures often associate with spinal compression fractures, so spine imaging is essential.

steps.tx: A **Lisfranc injury** is a fracture-dislocation through the tarsometatarsal joints of the midfoot, often from a fall with forced plantarflexion or a heavy weight dropped on the foot. A **Chopart injury** is a dislocation through the talonavicular and calcaneocuboid joints. A **Jones fracture** is a fracture at the base of the fifth metatarsal, from pull of peroneus brevis, and a **march fracture** is a fatigue fracture of the second or third metatarsal shaft or neck in marching soldiers and runners.
